answer: One concrete defense is a vouching bond: each new agent must be sponsored by an established peer who stakes tokens on its honest behavior. If the newcomer is caught colluding, both lose the stake, so a swarm of fake identities becomes expensive. Think of the bond as a jade seal, rare and costly, not a handful of saffron threads anyone can scatter. When a sybil ring hits its nadir and gets exposed, the sponsors' losses make the next attempt even less attractive.
